needs_human.note: A trashed subtitle row left by an earlier version stays in Trash while its file keeps serving the video as a track. Purging it, by hand or through the trash purge loop, deletes that file and the video loses the track (decisions.md:58 observed this by hand). The dialog says only that the file will be deleted.; Restoring such a trashed row gives a card back until the next scan, which then removes the row without notice.; Dropping a subtitle row emits no `files.purged`. Intelligence catches up through the orphan purge in reconcile (indexer.py:477-484) because the scan emits `scan.complete`, but the row removed at upload.py:183 waits for the next reconcile, and knowledge rows naming the id are cleaned only by `files.purged` (addons/knowledge/app/routers/webhooks.py).; A folder containing only uploaded subtitles is listed as empty, while its directory and files stay on disk. `delete_folder` (fileops.py:918-944) does not touch the disk and removes the EmptyFolder row, so a later scan lists the folder again. The non-row subtitle files stay invisible throughout.; Skipping `scan.complete` also skips the `drive.structure_changed` WebSocket event that it maps to (event_hooks.py:150, :164). A detail page already open during a subtitle upload may therefore not refresh its track list. decisions.md:55 notes this case was not exercised.

A row renamed or created with a .srt or .vtt name is deleted at the next scan with its comments, history and tag links, while the file stays on disk (scanner.py:441-451).; A subtitle upload no longer emits scan.complete, so an adjacent .vtt reaches Intelligence only at the next reconcile (uploads.py:82-83).

A note link of the form `loft://<id>` to a previously uploaded subtitle row, which the editor used to create correctly, dangles silently once the startup scan drops that row.; A trashed subtitle row still deletes the real file on purge, including the automatic retention purge at backend/app/main.py:135-152, although that file is still served as the video's track until then. decisions.md:58 observed the manual purge. The row is the only way left to remove such a file from the UI.; A trashed subtitle row keeps naming its path after the file is carried away. If a later rename or move carries a sidecar back to that path, the trash purge deletes that file.; `movie.ja.srt` being both the bare track of `movie.ja.mp4` and the Japanese track of `movie.mp4` is recorded in known-issues.md, but which video owns it stays undefined.; Uploading a subtitle with no matching video stores a file with no card, no track and no removal path; the answer is still a 200 and the drawer shows it as complete.
